svg.text: Measuring single-replica capacity (lambda_max) before any characterization run
SPEC.md §10; internal/calibrate.
One replica, addressed directly by its pod IP (no Service routing), with the experiment's
pins and load shape: Poisson arrivals, fixed input length, max_tokens = 256 with ignore_eos,
unique prefixes
Coarse ramp: run one step, starting at 2 requests per second
Did the step pass?
double
the rate
yes
no
Was it the 2 requests per second step?
calibration
invalid: no
lambda_max
yes
no
Fine ramp from the last passing rate r: r + 10 % of r,
r + 20 % of r, and so on, each step adding the same
10 % of r, until a step fails
lambda_max = the highest passing rate
The whole procedure runs twice
Do the two values differ by more than 10 %
of the larger?
no: lambda_max is the lower of the two
yes: a third ramp; lambda_max is the median
lambda_r = 0.65 x lambda_max, frozen for all N = 5 runs of both variants. The Service is offered
2 x lambda_r, so after the fault the survivor runs at 130 % of lambda_max.
The full trace is published: every step's rate, goodput and queue-gauge series
Each step
30 s settle, discarded, then 120 s measured.
The step passes if and only if, over the
measured portion:
• goodput is at least 99 %,
• the mean of the vLLM waiting-queue gauge
is at most 1.0, and
• the §2 client-validity gate is clean.
The queue mean counts only when at least 90 %
of the samples expected at the pinned cadence
landed inside the measured portion. A step short
of that is not judged: the procedure stops as an
execution error recorded in the trace.
Recalibration happens only when a §6 pin
changes, and is recorded.
